caption:
Until recently, only one organization launched rockets from India. Now a private startup just became the country's first space-tech unicorn.

Skyroot Aerospace hit a $1.1 billion valuation in May 2026, after raising $60 million - bringing its total funding to $160 million. Its rocket, Vikram-1, can carry up to 350 kilograms into low Earth orbit, built entirely by a private Indian company.

Over 100 authorizations have now been issued to private space companies in India, with more than $870 million invested in the sector. A bigger rocket, Vikram-2, capable of carrying nearly 900 kilograms, is already planned for 2027.

This isn't just one company's milestone. It's proof that India's space industry no longer needs to be built by one organization alone.

Sources: TechCrunch, SpaceNews, Orbital Today (2026)
